chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Bill Davis record with Duke Ellington
summary: Before Nat, Collins recorded Bill Davis's date with Jo Jones and Duke Ellington, who invited himself; it began the Bill Davis trio.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: During the time you were working steadily with Nat didn't you go record without Nat? (Inaudible).
I did some recordings with various -- with Bill (Inaudible) Davis.
Bill Davis, yes. This was before Nat.
I first heard it when I was with Nat.
Yeah, yeah. Bill Davis was going to

produce his own record, and he wanted -- he asked me to do it with him, yes. Here I was working at Birdland with someone then. So only -- you know who was on the date. It was Jo Jones, Duke Ellington and myself. Right? And "things aint' what they used to be." There were some good things.
Yeah, that's right. As a matter of fact he sold those, the masters to Mercury. And I think wasn't Mercer with Mercury at one time in some capacity? I don't know.

Yeah. But any way, this was the beginning of the Bill Davis trio. It was a trio, wasn't it. That Duke could -- you know, good old Duke, anything that was good he said, well, okay, I'll give you a boost. So he loved Bill Davis, you know.
So Bill told him he was going to -- this is -- I think Duke invited himself to the date. But it was a good record. You heard the record.
